# the contributor audit of the projection-recovery, peak, and arithmetic round



Read the full literal versions of:

* `candidate 5ef2792a4d153635`;
* `candidate d46094c158197e98`;
* `candidate 11867665f48c887c`;
* `candidate 5c9190df7c42c598`;
* `candidate 3b375252ca398671`;
* `candidate c7ae7f430666e631`.

For transformed recovery, orthogonalizing the image of the original
continuous subspace gives invertible diagonal blocks and preserves
the determinant used for coarse normalization. On each residual fine
fiber, the inverse s-Jacobian is |det C_i|^-1=M|det A_i|, so the
component covolume identity is exact, even with z-dependent coset
offsets. Uniform sampling applies to each lifted halfspace trace,
including an empty or full trace. The fine auxiliary measure is NOT
misidentified as an unweighted standard mixed measure. Interior
rounding occurs before the affine map back, and its fine-lattice
membership follows directly from the residual coset equation.
The necessary discarded-fine-mass hypothesis and the s=0 strict-gap
exception remain explicit. Added an explicit arbitrary-subsequence
paragraph to the universal liminf consequence; no other repair.

The sampled-peak proof uses only concavity of sampled roots and
unimodality. The adjacent minimum sum is exactly T-W, and the
polynomial interpolation integral contributes the claimed sharp
TV/(s+1) remainder. Equality in the weaker peak inequality is fully
proved using the TWO extreme fibers and BM equality, which forces
all intermediate fibers to be their affine translates. There is
no uncontrolled accumulation of pairwise translations. The N=0/N=1
and T=0 cases are separate; the endpoint identity was correctly
qualified to N>=1. Closed caps and open complements are treated
by compact exhaustion, monotone convergence, and a finite maximum,
so an entire sampled fiber on a boundary is counted once. The
J-level center is a genuine largest-volume fine-fiber centroid,
and the displayed J and coarse-volume restrictions are essential.

The kernel/module criterion uses deletion kernels rather than
requiring an empty whole convex hull. Integrality on the source
rows forces a kernel witness precisely as stated; simultaneous
character exclusion is stronger than separate nonzero classes.
The free-part prime argument is valid, and actual kernel classes
are in fact torsion because their rows lie in the rational span
of the source rows. The special thirteen-point forced row identity
is correct and does not imply the now-refuted universal bound.

For the eleven-point graph counter, the two nonvertex minimal faces
are y=0 and x=2. The explicit affine height prescriptions agree
where required and cover ALL anchored representations. The nine
exposing normals, the two disjoint midpoint pairs, and the y+z
separation of the outlier give a direct exact kernel certificate.
Projection plus Jensen affinity proves absence of extra integer
graph points. The remaining midpoint within the ten-point T rules
out a size-ten witness, establishing h(T)=9 exactly. The affine
basis at height zero and a height-one point prove full graph rank.

In the simplex-depth version, every W fiber is exactly K, the
exposed outlier is exactly a point, and the fractional-height coarse
fiber is exactly K but is NOT fine-sampled. The ambient hull is full
dimensional and equals conv(S). The finite cap cover has exactly
Gamma_s V mass in each positive cap and a zero-mass cap for the
outlier; an own-fiber centroid gives the matching lower bound.
The strict Gamma comparison follows from the displayed positive
second derivative for ALL real t>0, not from finite tests. The
actual fine OC target uses four integer variables and is not
contradicted.

For the original rank-budget seed, the enumerated nine integer
points and four nonvertex minimal faces give the two components
without relying on a numerical hull claim. The determinant -8
proves full rank of the large component. Cartesian products of
component equivalence relations give exact product components,
so the rank-cost ratio amplification (9/8)^q is valid and rules
out every fixed multiplier in that proposed allocation scheme.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
